analytics_user_data.instructions: This state is one analytics emission site: either a call that sends an event, or the declaration of an event's parameters. `site` is that code; `lines_above` is where its values come from. Judge only the values this site sends, not the rest of the change. Two things decide it, and both are about the value, never about what the field is called. First, where the value comes from: ScreenName.home and box.category.name are both "a name", and only one of them was written by the person using the app. Second, whether the value still carries that content when it is sent: an expression may READ something the person wrote and send only a fact about it — whether it is empty, how long it is, which bucket a count falls in — and a fact about the text is not the text. Ask what someone reading the event in the analytics dashboard would learn. If they would see something the person wrote, named or photographed, answer yes. If all they would see is how many, how long, how big, which of our own enum cases, or whether something was present, answer no.

criteria.true: At least one value sent here carries, in the event itself, content that the person using the app produced — a category or box name they typed, a note's title or body, a file name or path, a search term, an album name, a photo's local identifier, or a string that interpolates any of those.
criteria.false: Every value sent here is a count, a duration, a size in bytes, a boolean, a case of an enum declared in this app's own source, the rawValue of such an enum, an error code or error type name, a screen name, a store catalogue identifier chosen by the developer, or a fact derived from something the person wrote that does not carry its content — whether it is empty or present, its length, or which bucket it falls in.
